summary: As of November 24, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.72 percentage points and are up 0.29 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are up 0.06 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.80 percentage points. Of the 0.13 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.29 was the credit spread and 0.16 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 4.91 percent as of November 24, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.30 percent as of November 24, 2026, a gap of 0.39 percentage points. Brent is 91.01 dollars a barrel as of November 25, 2026 (-1.02 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.13 percent as of November 25, 2026, down 0.10 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.79 percent as of November 24, 2026. The broad dollar index is 123.60 as of November 20, 2026, +2.25 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 26.80 as of November 26, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.74 trillion dollars as of November 18, 2026, down 12 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 2.98 trillion dollars as of November 18, 2026, up 17 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.3 billion dollars as of November 25, 2026, down 0.105 billion over the latest four observations.
